2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 83 of 1998 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Sadar Gopalgonj impleading the petitioner and 3 others as defendants praying for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from entering into the suit land and from constructing any dormitory upon dispossessing the plaintiffs without payment of compensation money. In the said suit the plaintiff filed an application for temporary injunction. The learned Assistant Judge found that the plaintiff earlier obtained a contested decree in Title Suit. No. 69 of 1995 against the Government and that Title Appeal No. 71 of 1996 filed by the Government against the aforesaid decree was dismissed. The Government did not proceed further in the matter. The trial court accordingly found that the plaintiff' has a prima facie case and the plaintiff cannot be evicted from the suit land for the construction of any dormitory without payment of compensation to the plaintiffs. Accordingly by order dated 9.6.96 the learned Assistant Judge directed the parties to maintain status quo in respect of the suit land. Against the said order the Government filed Misc. Appeal No. 28 of 1998 before the learned District Judge, Gopalgonj. The learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gopalgonj who heard the said appeal found that the Government violated the fundamental right by not serving any notice upon the plaintiff before acquisition of the suit land and therefore the order of status quotes should be maintained. The lower appellate court also found that the defendant No. 4 Executive Engineer P.W.D. started the construction work upon violation of the courts order of status quo, therefore, departmental proceeding should be taken against him. The lower appellate court further found that alleged acquisition without payment of compensation auction is not permissible and the same is illegal and unauthorised. Accordingly by judgment and order the lower appellate court dis-missed the appeal and affirmed the decision of the trial court. 

 4. No one appears in support of the rule, while Mr. Shamsul Huda the learned Advocate appears to oppose the rule. I have perused the impugned order of the courts below arid the materials available on record. The plaintiffs title was established in Title Suit No. 65 of 1995 in the suit land. The Government preferred an appeal which was dismissed. The trial Court, therefore, found clear prima facie ease of title and possession in favour of the plaintiff. The Government case is that they acquired the suit land thereby the Government admits that the Government was not in possession of the suit land. In order to comply with the provision of acquisition of properties of the citizen, it is a mandatory provision that a notices is to be served on the owner or persons in possession of the property to be acquired and must be given an opportunity of being heard. Further it is established statutory provision that there cannot be any acquisition of any property without payment of compensation to the owner or persons concerned. The trial court appears to have rightly directed the parties to maintain status quo till payment of compensation of the land ought to be acquired. The High Court Division at the time of issuance of the rule directed "However pending hearing of the rule the work of construction of the dormitory for the purpose of accommodation of the Government officials shall proceed and it is not stayed. "It appears to me that the defendant-Government-petitioner was given the whole relief by allowing construction of the dormitory- and nothing remained to be decided in the rule itself. On the face of the view taken by the learned Judge at the time of issuance of the rule, it appears that the learned Judge found that there is an arguable case and thus a rule was issued to consider the legality and correctness of the order status quo passed by both the courts below. It was necessary that the status quo be maintained during pendency of the rule. Before, showing cause and without hearing the other side the Government should not have been allowed to construct the dormitory.
